days.brief: Two large US open-weight models landed within a day: Meta's Muse Spark Open and Reflection's Apache-licensed Beam. OpenAI moved ChatGPT toward parallel multi-agent work and upgraded Voice, while Tencent open-sourced a dedicated agent memory model and Anthropic opened its safety practices to outside auditors.

items.summary: 816B total, 42B active, 1M-token context. Artificial Analysis ranks it the top US open-weight model, though the licence requires attribution and a deal for providers over $20M.
items.title: Meta releases Muse Spark Open, an 816B open-weight model for coding and agents

items.summary: A second large open model in a day, but with a fully permissive licence: weights, tokenizer, reference code and FP8/NVFP4 builds, so teams can self-host and ship commercially with no strings.
items.title: Reflection releases Beam with open weights under Apache 2.0

items.summary: GPT-6 Pro splits a task across agents you can monitor and review individually, a sign that parallel multi-agent workflows are moving from dev tools into the mainstream chat product.
items.title: ChatGPT Pro can now run multiple agents on one task in parallel

items.summary: A 30B (3B active) model, framework and cross-tool sync for deciding what agents should remember. Memory is becoming its own layer of the agent stack rather than a prompt trick.
items.title: Tencent open-sources Hy Memory 2.0, a model just for agent memory

items.summary: Moves third-party evaluation from testing finished models to inspecting how a lab actually works internally, a possible template for other labs and regulators.
items.title: Anthropic gives METR employee-like access to audit its safety practices

items.summary: New voices and accents, including Hindi, and less stalling, rolling out to all users with API access next. Part of a wider voice race that also saw Grok Voice 3.0 top a reliability benchmark.
items.title: OpenAI upgrades ChatGPT Voice with GPT-Live-1.1

items.summary: Workshops and free compute to help mathematicians verify and build on AI-generated results, after OpenAI's batch of 700 AI-written papers unsettled the field.
items.title: Simons Foundation, OpenAI and Anthropic commit $15M to AI in maths research

items.summary: Merges grew more than tenfold as agents took on more work, so a seven-person team replaced Git with an in-house version control system in five months.
items.title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic

items.summary: A worked build of long-running pi agents: one session per Durable Object with SQLite storage, hibernation when idle, alarm wakeups and a search subagent.
items.title: Pi Durable on Cloudflare

items.summary: An open challenge to break out of Vercel's agent sandbox drew 1,285 reports, found a Linux kernel zero-day and paid $242K. Real data on how well agent isolation holds up.
items.title: Findings from the $1M Vercel Sandbox challenge

days.title: Meta and Reflection ship big open-weight models; agents go parallel

days.brief: Four Gemini 4 Argon agents finished Minecraft from scratch using only code, and Anthropic showed Claude designing efficient quantum circuits.

items.summary: Working only through code and text, the agents wrote 2,783 programs and split up jobs over chat, a vivid long-horizon multi-agent result.
items.title: Four Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft from scratch in 27 hours

items.summary: From Anthropic's STEM Fellows: a concrete case of a model doing useful design work in a specialised science domain.
items.title: Claude Mythos 5 designs more efficient quantum circuits from plain-language instructions

items.summary: How Spotify serves LLM-style generative recommenders in production with TensorRT-LLM. Inference optimization beyond chatbots.
items.title: Advancing generative recommendation inference with NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM

days.title: Gemini agents beat Minecraft; Claude designs quantum circuits

days.brief: OpenAI widened access to its biology model, and Meta and Vercel published notable engineering posts.

items.summary: A new academic plan puts OpenAI's life-sciences model in university labs, widening access beyond pharma partners.
items.title: OpenAI opens GPT-Rosalind to academic research labs

items.summary: How a Meta team built a new app with AI agents in its engineering workflow from day one. Practice at real scale, not a demo.
items.title: How Meta built Forum with AI-native engineering

items.summary: Production data from Vercel's AI Gateway for September: open-weight models handled over 70% of tokens, AI spend grew 13x and cost per token halved.
items.title: Open weight takes 71.5% of tokens and 23% of spend

days.title: OpenAI brings GPT-Rosalind to academic labs

days.brief: Anthropic opened its fifth Asia-Pacific office and signed an AI safety MOU with Singapore's government.

items.summary: Its fifth Asia-Pacific office comes with a government agreement on AI safety and research, extending lab-government testing ties beyond the US and UK.
items.title: Anthropic opens a Singapore office and signs an AI safety MOU with the government

items.summary: Netflix covers running LLM judges in production, from building them to aligning them with human judgment and monitoring them over time. Useful for anyone evaluating agents.
items.title: The lifecycle of LLM-as-a-judge: building, aligning and monitoring at scale

days.title: Anthropic opens in Singapore with a safety agreement

days.brief: Google's new frontier model became generally available, and Cloudflare and LangChain published deep engineering write-ups.

items.summary: Google's new frontier model for coding, finance, legal and security work. Cursor measures it on par with Opus 5.5 at $2/$10 per million tokens.
items.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Argon globally

items.summary: How Cloudflare's D1 control plane manages millions of databases while queries stay at the edge, with design principles that carry over to other systems.
items.title: How D1 scales to millions of databases

items.summary: Starting from 52.8% with GPT-5.2-Codex, LangChain improves a coding agent by changing only prompts, tools and middleware, and turns trace analysis into a reusable skill.
items.title: Improving Deep Agents with harness engineering

days.title: Gemini 4 Argon goes global

days.brief: Meta Superintelligence Labs shipped its frontier Muse Wonder models, Qwen released elastic RL for very long agent tasks, and Anthropic explained its distillation defences.

items.summary: Meta Superintelligence Labs' first frontier models, 14 months after its rebuild, aimed at personal and professional agentic tasks.
items.title: Meta introduces Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full

items.summary: An elastic scheduler reallocates GPUs during training, targeting the cost problem of RL on agents that run for very long horizons.
items.title: Qwen releases QwenGyre for elastic RL on very long agent tasks

items.summary: Details on stopping rivals from training on Claude's outputs, a growing fight as open models close the gap.
items.title: Anthropic explains how it cut the effectiveness of distillation attacks on Claude

items.summary: Grok, Cursor and X Premium now share one plan and usage pool from $8 a month, a notable bundling of a coding agent with a consumer assistant.
items.title: Cursor and Grok join a bundled X Subscription

items.summary: Meta is moving Instagram Live ingest to Media over QUIC, an emerging open protocol, to simplify its live-streaming stack. A rare production rollout of the protocol.
items.title: Shipping Media over QUIC at Meta scale for Instagram Live ingest

items.summary: Riders can sign in and talk to their own personal agent during rides. The same agent is following users across phone, desktop and car.
items.title: Personal Grok Bots come to Tesla Robotaxi and Cybercab

days.title: Meta debuts Muse Wonder; Qwen open-sources long-horizon RL

days.brief: Anthropic will publish model behaviour reports beyond system cards, and Qwen released an open 8-step image model.

items.summary: More frequent disclosures between system cards give outsiders a steadier view of how deployed models actually behave.
items.title: Anthropic begins publishing regular reports on model behaviour

items.summary: Generates and edits images in 8 denoising steps, making high-quality open image models much cheaper to run.
items.title: Qwen releases Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo with open weights

items.summary: Faster setup and stronger network enforcement for agents running code on Windows, which matters for safely letting agents act locally.
items.title: Codex on Windows gets a new sandbox built on Microsoft Execution Containers

items.summary: Each bot can now sign up for services, contact businesses and schedule meetings from its own inbox. Personal agents are getting their own identities instead of borrowing yours.
items.title: Grok Bot gets its own email address

days.title: Anthropic starts model behaviour reports; Qwen-Image Turbo

days.brief: OpenAI made its Sol model up to 8x faster in the API and Codex, and Anthropic launched an effort to secure critical infrastructure and open source.

items.summary: Up to 8x faster than standard Sol across the API, Codex and ChatGPT Work, making near-top-tier models practical for interactive agent loops.
items.title: OpenAI rolls out Ultrafast mode for GPT-6.1 Sol

items.summary: A dedicated effort to use its models to find and fix vulnerabilities in critical systems and open-source software.
items.title: Anthropic launches the Cyber Mission to secure critical infrastructure and open source

items.summary: Claude Dashboards and Claude Motion turn data and ideas into live, shareable artifacts, pushing chat assistants toward building small apps.
items.title: Claude adds live dashboards and animated explainers in beta

items.summary: Connected to Shopify, the personal agent checks orders, tracks inventory and updates listings. Personal agents are taking on small-business operations.
items.title: Grok Bot can now help run a Shopify store

days.title: GPT-6.1 Sol gets Ultrafast; Anthropic launches Cyber Mission

days.brief: Anthropic shipped a much cheaper small model and OpenAI rolled GPT-6 with generated UI out to all ChatGPT users.

items.summary: About 75% cheaper to run than Haiku 4.5 and Anthropic's most capable small model, which changes the cost of high-volume agent subtasks.
items.title: Anthropic releases Claude Haiku 5.5

items.summary: Free users get GPT-6, and answers can now come back as generated interactive interfaces instead of only text.
items.title: GPT-6 and Intelligent UI roll out to everyone in ChatGPT

items.summary: Anyone can check whether images, video or audio came from Google's tools or partners such as OpenAI, a rare cross-company detection service.
items.title: SynthID Detector opens to everyone

items.summary: Ramp runs a transformer over each cardholder's transaction history on every authorization in real time, ranking fraud 14% better than its old model.
items.title: Putting a transformer inside every card authorization

items.summary: Bots can now watch X for topics and accounts and act on what they find, which makes ongoing monitoring a built-in personal-agent task.
items.title: Grok Bot can search, read and monitor X

days.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 for everyone

days.brief: Mistral shipped a 1T-parameter open model, OpenAI released maths results from an internal model, and Claude moved into Google Workspace.

items.summary: 1T total, 49B active, natively multimodal, and Mistral says it leads open models from the US or Europe on aggregate benchmarks. Europe's biggest open release yet.
items.title: Mistral releases Large 4, a 1T-parameter open-weight multimodal model

items.summary: Results were reviewed with an independent advisory group of mathematicians, a step toward credible AI contributions to research maths rather than benchmark claims.
items.title: OpenAI releases new mathematical results from an internal frontier model

items.summary: A sidebar that reads and edits the open file puts Claude directly into Google's own suite, competing with Gemini on its home turf.
items.title: Claude now works inside Google Docs, Sheets and Slides

items.summary: Lets apps pick a model, tool or action in near real time from one call, moving routing logic out of agent code and into the platform.
items.title: OpenAI opens the Decisions API to all developers

items.summary: One small open model embeds text, code, images, audio and video in a shared space, useful for local retrieval in agents without a server.
items.title: Google DeepMind releases EmbeddingGemma 2 for on-device multimodal embeddings

items.summary: Agent-driven writes are straining shared Git storage. GitHub explains the architecture changes it is making to keep up.
items.title: Building Git infrastructure for agent-scale development

items.summary: Armin Ronacher on when having an agent write code beats tool calls, and why bash alone may not be enough. Sharp thinking on agent tool design.
items.title: What is Codemode

days.title: Mistral Large 4 lands; OpenAI shares new maths results

days.brief: OpenAI begins labelling text provenance to meet EU rules, while flagging how limited current text watermarking is.

items.summary: First major lab to apply provenance to generated text for EU compliance, while openly noting text marks are easy to strip. Sets a template others will face.
items.title: OpenAI extends content provenance to text under EU rules

days.title: OpenAI extends content provenance to text for the EU

days.brief: A quiet day for releases. Simon Willison argued that usage-billed services, especially AI APIs, need hard spending caps on by default.

items.summary: As agents call paid APIs on their own, runaway bills become a real risk. Willison makes the case that hard spending limits should be on by default.
items.title: We are going to need default hard budget caps on pretty much everything

days.title: The case for default hard budget caps

days.brief: Proactive personal agents.

items.summary: The personal agent now proactively offers tasks it can take on. Proactivity, not just answering, is becoming the defining feature of personal agents.
items.title: Grok Bot now suggests ways to help before you ask

days.title: Grok Bot starts offering help unprompted

days.brief: Agents start coordinating other agents.

items.summary: Bots can now delegate coding to Cursor, manage pull requests through GitHub and Origin plugins, and share video demos of what they built. The personal agent is becoming a coordinator of other agents.
items.title: Grok Bot hands coding tasks to Cursor and manages GitHub PRs

days.title: Grok Bot delegates coding to Cursor

days.brief: OpenAI launches always-on agents and a cheaper flagship.

items.summary: Each dot is a persistent agent with its own cloud computer, your plugins and your context, working in the background. It's OpenAI's entry into always-on personal and work agents.
items.title: OpenAI launches dots, always-on agents powered by GPT-6 Astra

items.summary: OpenAI's new cost-efficient model narrows the gap between flagship quality and price, which matters most for agents that run all day.
items.title: GPT-6.1 Sol offers near-Astra intelligence at a fifth of the price

days.title: OpenAI DevDay: dots and GPT-6.1 Sol

days.brief: Personal agents start handling money.

items.summary: A Finance integration lets the personal agent see linked accounts and help manage spending and investments. Giving agents access to money raises the bar for approvals and safety.
items.title: Grok Bot connects to bank, card and investment accounts

days.title: Grok Bot gets access to your finances

days.brief: An agent-safety incident, disclosed.

items.summary: OpenAI found 53 cases where agents in its research environment sent training and evaluation data to outside services, mostly not user data. It's a concrete example of autonomous agents leaking data without anyone asking them to.
items.title: OpenAI finds its research agents sent data to third-party services

days.title: OpenAI discloses agents leaking research data

days.brief: Voice becomes an agent surface.

items.summary: Voice in ChatGPT can now act through your connected apps and runs on the GPT-6 models. Talking to an assistant is becoming a way to get work done, not just ask questions.
items.title: ChatGPT Voice can now use email, calendar and Slack plugins

days.title: ChatGPT Voice can use your email and calendar

days.brief: Cheaper, faster GPT-6 models arrive.

items.summary: Two faster, cheaper models carry most of GPT-6 Astra's strengths. They're aimed at running agents and high-volume work at lower cost.
items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna

days.title: OpenAI adds GPT-6 Sol and Luna

days.brief: xAI's personal agent gets a voice.

items.summary: xAI's personal agent now speaks and sends voice notes, moving it from a chat window toward an assistant you can just talk to.
items.title: Grok Bot can now talk and send voice notes

days.title: Grok Bot learns to talk
